messages:
Alex C: Quick follow-up from the kernel RFC — CI started failing on the new attention kernel build, looks like fatbin sizes spiked and the size gate blocked the artifact. paste of the failing line: `ERROR: artifact size 312MB > gate 256MB`

Jin L: I saw that. The new kernels generate PTX for multiple architectures by default. nvcc is emitting ptx+fatbin for sm_86,sm_90,sm_100 in our matrix which doubles the fatbin.

Mike R: Can we change nvcc flags to avoid redundant PTX in the release build? e.g. `-gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86 -gencode=arch=compute_90,code=sm_90` but drop `-ptx` output or set `--ptxas-options=-v`?

Jin L: A few levers: 1) limit gencode list to only supported SMs for that image, 2) use `--fatbin=false`/explicit `-cubin` where possible, 3) set `-Xptxas --version`/`--gpu-architecture=sm_86` to control ptx version, 4) split objects per-sm and link only needed ones.

Sara P: CI-wise we should avoid changing the global toolchain until we have a safe fallback. Options: add an arch whitelist per build matrix (fast), or add a post-build step to strip PTX sections we don't need (risky), or change the size gate to be per-variant rather than global (cheaper but possibly hides real regressions).

Elena (pm): What is lowest-risk path for the next release? We need a hotfix to get CI green, then a longer-term plan.

Mike R: Hotfix idea: add a short script in the CI job that runs `nvdisasm`/`cuobjdump` to detect unused PTX sections and remove them from the fatbin. Practically easier: build with `-Xlinker --strip-all` on non-debug builds, and validate cpu/gpu tests unaffected.

Jin L: Stripping symbols helps, but PTX sections remain. We could run `cuobjdump --dump-ptx` and then `llvm-nm` to check references — if no references to higher-sm kernels, we can safely drop. But that's a lot of scripting.

Alex C: Would a whitelist per-image be acceptable? CI build matrix can pass an env var like ARCH_WHITELIST=sm_86,sm_90 and we reduce gencodes accordingly. That should shrink artifacts quickly.

Sara P: Yes, whitelist is fastest. We should also add a test job that intentionally builds the full matrix and uploads to an internal bucket so we detect size regressions without blocking primary CI. Non-blocking job lives in eng-runtime-nightly.

Mike R: For long-term: consider splitobj + LTO for smaller linked artifacts, and a unified artifact layout where per-sm micro-libs are pulled on demand by the runtime. That needs distro changes.

Jin L: Also watch PTX version drift — newer toolkits produce larger PTX. We can normalize with `-ptxinfo` settings and force `--generate-code arch=compute_86,code=compute_86` for PTX-only variants.

Elena (pm): Action items?

Alex C: I propose: 1) Hotfix: implement ARCH_WHITELIST in CI and update release pipeline (Mike + Jin) — target: today. 2) Add non-blocking full-matrix nightly build that uploads size reports (Sara) — target: this week. 3) RFC follow-up for splitobj/LTO and runtime micro-libs (Alex + Jin) — target: next sprint.

Mike R: I can push the ARCH_WHITELIST change in a tiny patch, will add a fallback to default to the old gencode list if var is unset.

Jin L: I'll prototype a small cuobjdump-based filter for later; will post results in this thread.

deploy-bot: build/eng-runtime-pr-482: failed — artifact size 312MB (limit 256MB).

Sara P: Thanks everyone. Ping me when the whitelist patch is up and I'll kick a release build. :thumbsup:
